clue.text: Arc lamp set off material for reprocessing

indicators.note: off here means set going wrong or disordered, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets off an arc lamp, and the scene drifts into salvage talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' looks like a phrase meaning 'triggered', but 'set' belongs to the fodder and 'off' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap metal is waste iron or steel collected to be melted down and reused, so it is exactly stuff for recycling.

clue.text: Perversion is welcomed by unhappy male

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by the following words

parts.note: unhappy means sad

explanation.surface: An unhappy man accepts some deviant behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking pleasure in inflicting pain is a form of sexual or moral deviance.

clue.text: Government, for example, finding itself constricted by frost

indicators.note: constricted by means squeezed inside the next word

parts.note: rime is hoar frost
EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A government gripped by a cold spell, metaphorical or literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a system or particular administration that rules a country.

clue.text: 9, apparently, that should help fix a broken leg

definitions.meaning: the clue numbered 9 is a sauce of salad oil; taken literally it would be a bandage from France's capital

definitions.text: that should help fix a broken leg
definitions.meaning: a quick-setting white gypsum used to make casts for fractured limbs

explanation.surface: A cross-reference joke about salad sauce turning medical.
explanation.walkthrough: 9-down is FRENCH DRESSING: read literally, a dressing (bandage) that is French, i.e. from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: This gypsum material sets hard and was traditionally used to make casts to immobilise broken bones.

clue.text: Alienated journalist full of rum

indicators.note: full of means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
rum is an old British word for strange or odd

explanation.surface: A journalist drunk on rum has fallen out with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but it is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Being estranged is being no longer close or friendly, cut off from someone.

clue.text: Set aside a great deal for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means as heard by listeners, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: A generous portion is reserved for the spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to assign or apportion something for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Look after contents of lost city

indicators.note: after says the next piece comes behind the one before it
contents of a word are its inside letters, leaving off the first and last

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone asks a friend to look after the belongings of a lost town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as 'care for', but the two words split: 'Look' is a piece and 'after' only places it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital is a city, so the plain one-word definition fits.

clue.text: Rising role adopted by stars in hot spots

indicators.note: adopted by means taken inside the following word

parts.note: suns are stars

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read upwards, so the role word is turned around

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming part is taken on by celebrities in fashionable venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests celebrities and 'hot spots' trendy venues, but the stars are astronomical and the spots literally sunny.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered sunny places that catch the warmth are literally spots that get hot.

clue.text: Covers, but hams it up ignoring head of production

indicators.note: ignoring means the next letter is left out

parts.note: an actor who hams it up overplays

indicators.note: head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An understudy covers, but overacts, regardless of the director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring head of production' drops the P from OVERPLAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlays are layers placed on top of something, coatings that cover it.

clue.text: European resigns in confusion after daughter shows sauce

indicators.note: after places the scrambled letters behind the daughter letter

parts.note: a French person is a European

indicators.note: in confusion means the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A European quits in a muddle after his daughter cheeks him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' looks like cheek, but it is the definition: a vinaigrette.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinaigrette of oil and vinegar is a salad sauce.

clue.text: Follow Master of Arts principle

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
MA is the abbreviation for the degree Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Advice to adopt the guiding principle of someone with an arts degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a firmly held principle or tenet laid down as true.

clue.text: Understanding the ability to resist pain

definitions.meaning: being understanding of others means accepting and forgiving their differences
a high pain threshold, the capacity to endure discomfort or a drug's effects

explanation.surface: A sympathetic person is described as also being able to bear pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both forbearance toward others and physical endurance of pain or stress.

clue.text: Island craft backed by whole area

parts.note: a sum is a whole, a total

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the word for craft is read in reverse

parts.note: craft means skill or art

explanation.surface: A boat sits beside a whole region of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a boat, but here it means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large island of Indonesia.

clue.text: Shoot and frighten drill-sergeant to a limited extent

indicators.note: to a limited extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to shoot at and scare a drill-sergeant, but only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a verb to go with 'frighten', but it is a noun, a plant's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender shoot by which a climbing plant clings.

clue.text: Showing pleasure after trip, but too gung-ho?

indicators.note: after puts the pleasure word behind the trip word

parts.note: to trip a mechanism is to set it off, to trigger it
someone showing pleasure is happy

explanation.surface: Someone delighted after a journey may be over-eager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' suggests a holiday, but here it is the verb to set off a mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick to shoot or act rashly is being overly keen and reckless, like a gunslinger.

clue.text: Worn out as he taxed us horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a tax collector has drained everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exhausted means being completely tired, drained of energy.

clue.text: Set out carrying load to get continental delicacy

indicators.note: carrying means the outer letters hold the next word inside
out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: cargo is a load carried by ship or plane

explanation.surface: Someone sets off with a load, aiming for a European treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of 'Set' to EST, which is then split around the load.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible snails are a French speciality, a delicacy of the Continent.

clue.text: Well-made goods from Germany and Belarus ordered

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Quality goods are ordered from two European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like 'bought', but signals the rearrangement of BELARUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Durables are long-lasting consumer goods such as appliances, built to last.

clue.text: Feeling full, runs into this silly pompous ass

parts.note: after a big meal one feels stuffed

indicators.note: into says the runs letter goes inside the word this
silly suggests jumbled, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket scoresheet abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An overfed person runs into a foolish, self-important twit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside THIS, and 'silly' rearranges THRIS to make the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed shirt is an idiom for a pompous, conventional, self-important person.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader's shed with room, oddly

parts.note: to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters only

explanation.surface: A rebel leader owns an outbuilding with an unusual room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led the Cuban revolution and then the country.

clue.text: Give up bad habits seeing case of reserve on bench

indicators.note: case of a word is its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: a form is a long wooden bench, as in a school

explanation.surface: A substitute sitting on the bench decides to change his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve on bench' evokes a sports substitute; FORM is an old schoolroom bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to mend one's ways and become better behaved.

clue.text: Computer images a sailor's found linked to the Bible

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
a tar is a sailor; the possessive gives TAR'S

explanation.surface: A seaman's computer graphics turn out to be connected with scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the King James, or Authorised Version, of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatars are the graphical figures representing users in games and online.

clue.text: Step from prison to accept first of awards

indicators.note: to accept means the prison word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

indicators.note: first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A step up from jail to receiving prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is one of a flight of steps.

clue.text: Steal the limelight from leading coach

parts.note: up means ahead or leading, as in a game
a stage is a stagecoach

explanation.surface: Someone takes the attention away from the main trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a trainer, but here it is a horse-drawn stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine someone and draw attention away from them is the idiom here.

clue.text: Eight pints not on? Then four with soldier and run around for fun

indicators.note: not says the word on is left out of the measure

parts.note: a gallon holds eight pints
IV is four in Roman numerals
a soldier ant is a worker ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: A drinker turns down eight pints, then goes off with four friends and a soldier for a lark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' tells you to drop ON from GALLON, leaving GALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to roam about in search of pleasure.

clue.text: Keen on covering Queen's opening bars?

indicators.note: covering means the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: into is slang for keen on, as in into jazz
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A fan wants to cover the start of a Queen song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the rock band, but it gives R, for Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece of music, its first few bars.

clue.text: Job request following termination of employment

indicators.note: following puts the request word after the end letter
termination of a word is its last letter

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Someone makes a demand after losing their post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'termination of employment' reads as being sacked, but it just picks the last letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work, a job to be done.

clue.text: Union man's bedroom frolics with girl finishing early

indicators.note: frolics suggests playful jumping about, so the letters are rearranged
finishing early means the word stops short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A trade unionist larks about in the bedroom with a woman who leaves early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union man' looks like a trade unionist, but the union is a marriage. GIR is mixed with BEDROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The man getting married is joined in a marital union.
